newsitem.title: UK: French award threatens Brent Walker.
newsitem.headline: French award threatens Brent Walker.

text.p: Leisure group Brent Walker could face collapse after a French judge granted an award of six million stg in favour of the company's founder George Walker, The Times newspaper said.
The company immediately appealed against the decision, which could threaten the disposal of its Pubmaster public house chain and affect any future sale of William Hill, the betting chain.
"Brent Walker had previously threatened to place the company in receivership if the French action went in Mr. Walker's favour," the newspaper said.
Media reports said earlier this week that a group led by NatWest Ventures could emerge as the preferred bidder for Pubmaster in a deal worth over 165 million stg.
The Times said the French action relates to event in 1989, when Holt Freres, a Walker family trust, provided a loan of 250 million stg towards various French interests.

Half the sum was repaid, leaving Brent Walker with 10.2 million stg to repay. With interest the amount has risen to 18 million stg. The company has been struggling with huge debts and last week reported a half year pretax loss of 51.6 million stg and passed on its interim dividend.
